alternate_names: Sri Varahalakshmi Narasimha Swamy Vari Devasthanam

history.dynasty: Chola (Kulottunga I, earliest inscription 1087 CE); Eastern Ganga (Narasimhadeva I, 13th century - present stone temple, consecrated by Bhanudeva I in 1268 CE); Gajapati; Vijayanagara (Krishnadevaraya's visit and endowments, 1516-1519)
history.summary: One of Andhra Pradesh's most important Vishnu temples, on the Simhachalam hill range (~300 m above sea level) in the Eastern Ghats. Legend holds that Vishnu appeared here as Varaha Narasimha to save his devotee Prahlada from Hiranyakashipu; the idol (boar's head, human torso, lion's tail, 2.5 ft, no carved ornaments) is kept covered in sandalwood paste all year and revealed only for 12 hours on Akshaya Tritiya (Chandanotsavam). The Kalinga/Dravidian stone temple holds ~500 inscriptions; Vaishnavite saint Ramanuja visited in the 11th century, and practices follow the Pancharatra Agama while retaining Shaivite-tinged customs (a unique Vaishnavite-Shaivite blend). It is Andhra Pradesh's second-richest temple after Tirumala. name: Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Simhachalam is a hill suburb of Visakhapatnam in the Simhachalam hill range of the Eastern Ghats, about 300 metres above sea level. Part of the Greater Visakhapatnam municipal area, it is reached by a winding ghat road and draws pilgrims year-round to the hilltop temple, one of the 32 Narasimha Kshetras of Andhra Pradesh.

travel.road: APSRTC buses from Visakhapatnam RTC Complex (~20 km); scenic uphill ghat road to the hilltop; ~1000-step stairway from the foothills also available
